1/6 Calling external contracts can transfer control before your function finishes, allowing another contract to execute first.

2/6 This allows a malicious contract to call back into you before the original invocation completes.

3/6 Different invocations of the same function may then interact in undesirable ways.

4/6 To avoid this, perform all internal state changes before making any external calls.

5/6 This approach is known as the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern.

6/6 Alternatively, you can use a reentrancy lock like OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard.
